_about: New fields for the v3 team page. Merge each block into the matching seed file (or the real data source) by id, then extend the zod schemas in lib/data and data/schema. Every fact here comes from claims already in claims.json. Text marked draft needs a review by the team before launch. See UPDATE.md §9.

levels._field: plain: the one-line meaning shown in the rating-scale tooltip

clean.plain: We checked every sponsor on the shirt and found nothing.

spotted.plain: A lesser link, like a sponsor that a state partly owns.

stained.plain: A sponsor with a serious record on the front, or a severe one elsewhere on the shirt.

soaked.plain: A sponsor with a severe record on the front, or two serious ones.

sponsors._fields: ownerVerb: 'owned by' (default) or 'paid for by'. why.text: the 'Why is that a problem?' paragraph (draft). why.claimIds: the claims it rests on, shown as its source. why.messageLine: the one sentence used in the Tell-the-club draft message.

why.text: Dubai is part of the United Arab Emirates, where criticising the government can land you in prison. In 2024, 43 activists got life sentences in a single mass trial. Putting Emirates on a famous shirt makes the country look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: In 2024, 43 activists in the UAE got life sentences in one mass trial.

why.text: Rwanda’s government pays to put its tourism brand on the shirt. UN experts say 3,000–4,000 Rwandan troops are fighting alongside M23 rebels in eastern Congo, where the rebels take about $800,000 a month from coltan mining. A famous shirt makes Rwanda look like a holiday destination while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: UN experts say 3,000–4,000 Rwandan troops are fighting alongside M23 rebels in eastern Congo.

why.text: Riyadh Air belongs to Saudi Arabia’s state fund, which the crown prince chairs. Saudi Arabia carried out a record 345 executions in 2024, and US intelligence assessed that the crown prince approved the operation that killed journalist Jamal Khashoggi. A famous shirt makes the country look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: Saudi Arabia carried out a record 345 executions in 2024.

kits._fields: headline: the bold sentence under the club name; {level} is replaced by the level word in its level colour. Past kits use 'was'. shortLine: the one line in 'Travel back in time'. change.text replaces the existing text where given.

copy._about: Fixed strings for the v3 team page. {club}, {sponsor}, {n}, {level}, {period} are placeholders.

explainer.text: Behind the Jersey shows who really pays for the sponsors on a club’s shirt. We trace each sponsor to its owner, check the human-rights record behind the money, and rate the shirt on a four-step scale from Clean to Soaked.

sponsors.title: Every sponsor on the shirt
sponsors.sub: Click a row for the money and the evidence. The numbers match the shirt.
sponsors.unratedDetail: We haven’t traced who owns {sponsor} yet, so there is no rating. A rating only goes up once every claim is sourced.

act.title: What you can do
act.intro: You don’t have to stop supporting {club} or wearing the shirt. Sponsors do change, and fans speaking up is part of why: {examples}.

tell.title: Tell {club}
tell.text: It takes about two minutes. Send the club a short, polite message: we write the draft, you change what you like and send it from your own email to the club’s supporter liaison officer.
tell.draftEmpty: Tick a sponsor to see your message.

more.title: Share {club}’s status
more.text: Most fans don’t know who pays for their shirt. Share a card with the rating and the facts.

more.title: Bring it to your fan group
more.text: A supporters’ trust carries more weight than one email. Take a one-page fact sheet with every source.

more.title: Help check {sponsor}
more.text: We haven’t traced who owns {sponsor} yet. Anyone can add a source, and every one is checked.

more.title: Follow {club}
more.text: One email when the shirt changes or a sponsor deal comes up for renewal. Nothing else.

shirt.hint: Hover a number to find it in the list.

travel.title: Travel back in time
travel.sub: Click a season to see that shirt and its sponsors.
travel.pastNotice: You’re looking at an old shirt ({period}).

message._about: Draft for 'Tell {club}'. One sponsor paragraph per ticked sponsor, in list order.
message.subject: A question about our shirt sponsor
message.opening: I’ve supported the club for years and I’m proud of our shirt.
message.ask: Please don’t let our shirt be used to cover for that. When the deal is next reviewed, please look for a sponsor every fan can be proud of.
